statement: The Livonian Order (the Livonian Brothers of the Sword, founded 1202, absorbed into the Teutonic Order 1237) controlled Livonia and Estonia — the northeastern Baltic crusading territory — as a nominally subordinate branch of the Teutonic Order. In practice, the Livonian master operated with considerable independence, as the geographic separation from Prussia made direct control difficult. The Livonian Order suffered a catastrophic defeat at the Battle of the Ice (Lake Peipus, 1242) against Alexander Nevsky's Novgorodian forces, permanently halting expansion eastward. The Order dissolved with the Livonian Confederation's collapse (1561).
